title: Entropy-gated session mixer for adaptive streaming batches
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: For streaming chat completions we need a batching strategy that maximizes token throughput while preserving p95/p99 latency SLOs and avoiding KV cache thrashing on GPU memory. Current approaches either over-aggregate (high latency, KV churn) or underutilize GPU slabs (low throughput).

Proposal: Implement an "entropy-gated session mixer" that: (1) computes a lightweight per-session entropy score on recent token distributions and response lengths, (2) uses the entropy score to gate which sessions are allowed to be mixed in the same micro-batch, (3) adaptively sizes micro-windows based on observed sequence lengths and KV cache pressure, and (4) pins hot-session KV slots to a fast-resident region to avoid repeated eviction when mixing. The heuristic is designed to run in the request router/packetizer before slab packing and to emit metrics for tuning.

Why this approach: entropy approximates unpredictability of future token generation; mixing low-entropy sessions tends to yield similar sequence-length profiles and higher batching efficiency, while high-entropy sessions that are bursty or long are kept isolated or batched conservatively. Pinning hot KV entries prevents oscillation in the slab allocator and reduces serialization costs on rehydration.

Success criteria and measurable goals are below.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmarked microbench: throughput (tokens/sec) increases >= 12% on mixed workloads versus baseline greedy-batcher under equivalent load conditions
p95 latency regression <= 5% and p99 latency regression <= 2% compared to baseline under steady-state streaming SLOs
End-to-end KV cache hit ratio improves by >= 8% on representative production trace samples
GPU memory headroom (hosted as percent of total GPU) increases by >= 6% during peak simulated sessions
No correctness regressions in decoding output (SMOKE QA + regression prompt-suite pass)
Feature toggle and telemetry available in runtime-1.21 for canary rollout with metrics dashboard
implementation_steps: Design lightweight entropy estimator and validate correlation with sequence-length variance (prototype in simulator)
Integrate gating into request router: compute per-session entropy, label session as MIXABLE/HOT/ISOLATE
Micro-window sizing module: derive window sizes from running mean/variance of recent lengths and KV pressure signals
KV pinning proto: reserve hot-slot range within slab allocator and add fast-path checks in KV rehydration
Add slab-aware packer hooks to prefer mixable sessions co-located in contiguous slabs
End-to-end benchmarking harness: integrate with existing streaming simulator and perf dashboards
Safety net: implement fallback to existing latency-first batching policy if memory pressure or p99 breach detected
Write e2e tests, unit tests, and load tests; submit RFC and internal design doc for review
Canary rollout with telemetry and phased increase in traffic share, monitor, and iterate
experiments: Prototype (simulator) run 2026-02-25: entropy threshold sweep showed peak throughput at entropy=0.32; throughput delta +16% vs greedy on mixed trace (latency p95 +3%)
KV pinning microtest 2026-03-03: pinning top-10% hottest sessions reduced rehydrate calls by 27% in 2h trace
GPU memory profile 2026-03-07: slab fragmentation decreased 9% when using slab-aware packer with entropy gating
Fail-safe test 2026-03-10: induced memory spike triggered fallback within 1s and p99 stayed within SLO during simulated outage
decision_log: Chose Shannon-based moving-window entropy (128-token window) for compute simplicity and interpretability
Rejected strictly priority-only mixing because it caused hot-session starvation on long conversations
KV pinning uses soft reservations (best-effort) rather than hard allocation to avoid strict fragmentation
Pinned-slot fraction default = 8% of slab; will expose as config per customer tier
Fallback policy: latency-first greedy batcher with preemptive cache warm-up is the immediate fallback
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Entropy estimator misclassifies multimodal sessions -> Mitigation: use decay + hysteresis and require two consecutive windows before state change
Risk: Pinning leads to fragmentation -> Mitigation: soft reservation + periodic compaction during low-util windows
Risk: Added router CPU overhead -> Mitigation: move estimator to a short native extension or sample 1/4 sessions for full estimator
Risk: Unexpected model quality regressions -> Mitigation: run full regression prompt-suite and canary with human-in-the-loop review for first 48h
